title: CLAY COUNTY PROPERTY TAXES
full_story:
Clay County Real Estate tax bills will be mailed on Friday, September 11th.

The first installment of the 2025 taxes payable in 2026 is due Friday, October 16th.  The second installment is due on Friday, November 20th.

Payment can be made to the Clay County Treasurer using any of the following options, by mail, send your check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville, IL 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  You can pay at the treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse where they accept cash, checks, cashier’s checks, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  Office hours are 8:00 am – 4:00 pm Monday through Friday.  Online payments can be made by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC #a00082, there will be a convenience fee charged for online Credit Card payments.  Payment can also be made by placing your payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.

For questions call Clay County Treasurer Stacey Allen’s office at 618-665-3727.

title: IUKA MAN ARRESTED
full_story:
73-year-old Ray Krutsinger of Iuka was arrested for misdemeanor battery after allegedly pushing a man causing him to fall and then dragging him down the driveway by his belt.

Salem Police say Krutsinger had gone to a home on Allman Street late Tuesday afternoon to help someone move.  Another person asked him to leave, when the altercation allegedly occurred.  The alleged victim did not require hospital treatment.

Krutsinger was still at the home when police arrived and arrested him.  He was taken to the Marion County Jail where he was later released on a notice to appear.

title: WAYNE COUNTY CROP YIELD TOUR
full_story:
The 43rd annual Wayne County Farm Crop Yield Tour was completed on Monday.

Overall, the numbers for corn are 30 bushels per acre better than last year.  This year’s projected yield for corn is 200 bushels per acre.  That is up from 170 last year.  For soybeans, the numbers are up from a year ago.  This year’s projected yield for soybeans is 63 bushels per acre, up from 47 bushels per acre in 2025.

As for areas of the county, the southeast area shows the strongest numbers for corn averaging 216 bushels per acre.  The worst area was in the northwest with a projected yield of 181 bushels per acre.  As for soybeans, the southeast again led the way with a projected yield of 71 bushels per acre.  The low spot in the county is the northwest with a projected yield of 56 bushels per acre.

For corn the high was a field with a projected yield of 226 bushels per acre and a low of 168 bushels per acre.  For soybeans, the high was a field with a projected yield of 72 bushels per acre and a low of 53 bushels per acre.

In the history of the local tour, the lowest yields were in 1983 with 17.4 bushel soybeans and 34 bushel corn.

title: FIRST HUMAN CASE OF WNV
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH) confirmed the first human case of West Nile virus (WNV) in Illinois for 2026.  The confirmed case involves a resident of Piatt County.  In addition, IDPH has identified three other probable human cases of WNV from northern Illinois.  About one in five people who contract the disease caused by a bite from an infected mosquito may develop common symptoms, including fever, headache, body aches, joint pain, or other potentially serious complications.

So far in 2026, WNV has been observed in 50 Illinois counties with either a mosquito pool, horse and/or human from that county testing positive for the virus.  So far 2 mosquito batches in Clay County have tested positive for WNV.  The positive samples were collected in Louisville on July 24th and in Clay City on August 19th.

In 2025, WNV was found in 73 Illinois counties.  There was a total of 150 human cases, with ten deaths linked to the virus.

“For many Illinois residents, summer means lots of time spent outdoors enjoying everything our state has to offer,” said IDPH Director Dr. Sameer Vohra.  “Before heading outside, it’s important to take steps to protect yourself and loved ones from mosquito bites and the illnesses they can spread.  Applying insect repellant, wearing long, loose clothing, and reporting stagnant water to your local health department can help lower the risk of contracting diseases like West Nile Virus.”

IDPH urges the public to Fight the Bite by practicing the three “R’s” – reduce, repel, and report.

IDPH supports mosquito control efforts throughout the state by providing $2.8 million in funding to Illinois’ 97 local health departments for vector surveillance and control activities.  This includes purchasing and applying larvicide, working with municipal governments and local news media for WNV prevention and education, and investigating mosquito production sites and nuisance mosquito complaints.  Local health departments collect mosquitoes for West Nile virus testing.

Monitoring for WNV in Illinois includes tests for mosquito batches, as well as testing sick horses and humans with West Nile virus-like symptoms.

West Nile virus is transmitted through the bite of a Culex mosquito, commonly called a house mosquito, that has picked up the virus by feeding on an infected bird.  Common symptoms include fever, nausea, headache and muscle aches.  Symptoms may last from a few days to a few weeks.  Most people infected with West Nile virus will not show any symptoms; however, in rare cases it can lead to severe illness including paralysis, meningitis or encephalitis or even death.  People older than 60 and those with weakened immune systems are at highest risk for severe illness.

title: SI MADE EXPO
full_story:

title: CAREER DAY
full_story:
Lake Land College is hosting its annual Career Day event on Tuesday, October 6th.  The event will give high school juniors and seniors from 25 high school districts the chance to network with local professionals and discover rewarding career possibilities.

During this year’s Career Day event, participating students will choose from more than 150 scheduled sessions to attend to learn about a diverse range of local career paths.  Each session will provide an in-depth presentation from local professionals representing industries such as agriculture, healthcare, business, information technology, cosmetology, humanities, arts, communications, welding, math, science, engineering, education, criminal justice, human services, psychology, sociology, political science, history, automotive, construction, technology and more.

This year’s Career Day event will also include a Career and College Fair for students to attend before or after their scheduled sessions.  At the Career and College Fair, students will be able to meet with representatives from colleges and universities across the country to learn about programs, transfer options, scholarships and more.  Representatives from local businesses, as well as from all branches of the military, will also be present at the Career & College Fair to discuss apprenticeships, internships and additional career opportunities.

“There’s no better way to learn about possible career paths than by hearing the insights and perspectives of the people who work in those jobs every day,” said Peighton Hinote, Coordinator for Student Communication & Initiatives.  “This event is always a perfect opportunity for students to receive everything they need all in one place as they begin to make their future plans.”

Colleges, universities and local organizations interested in presenting during Career Day or hosting a table at the College and Career Fair can register by Friday, October 2nd on the Lake Land College website at LakeLandCollege.edu/Career-Day/College-Organization-Information/.

High school juniors and seniors interested in attending Career Day can contact Hinote at 217-234-5230 or [email protected].

For more information, visit the Lake Land College website at LakeLandCollege.edu/Career-Day.

title: ENERGY EFFICIENCY PROJECTS GRANTS
full_story:
Illinois Environmental Protection Agency (Illinois EPA) Director James Jennings Tuesday announced $766,600 in funding through the Public Buildings Energy Efficiency Program for projects that include energy efficiency upgrades identified in an energy efficiency assessment or audit conducted within the last five years.  The Efficient and Resilient Public Building Grant Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) is now posted.

“This program provides financial resources as well as technical support through Illinois EPA’s Office of Energy,” said Director Jennings.  “This funding will improve energy efficiency and provide cost savings to public buildings in Illinois.”

The Public Building Energy Efficiency Program provides financial assistance for energy efficiency improvements at public buildings owned by municipalities, counties, and other units of local government.  Energy efficiency is essential for reducing energy demand, conserving natural resources, and minimizing the environmental impacts associated with energy production.

Examples of eligible projects include building envelope insulation, window replacement lighting upgrades, programmable thermostats and occupancy sensors, heating and cooling system retrofit, high efficiency appliances, and a transfer switch.  An energy efficiency assessment or audit refers to a review of the property conducted by a third-party professional that results in recommendations at improving energy efficiency and/or reducing energy costs.

Grants will be capped at a maximum of $200,000 per grantee.  Funding is provided through the U.S. Department of Energy State Energy Program to Illinois.  The Notice of Funding Opportunity and additional information can be found at on Illinois EPA’s Office of Energy webpage.  Applications for the Efficient and Resilient Public Building Grant will be accepted through September 30th.  Applicants must apply through the Grant Accountability and Transparency Act Grantee Portal.

title: AVIATION EXPO RETURNS
full_story:
Aviation enthusiasts, pilots, prospective aircraft owners and anyone curious about the world of flight are invited to the Mt. Vernon Outland Airport (MVN) for the 18th Annual Midwest Aviation Expo (MAX), taking place Thursday, September 10th through Saturday, September 12th, from 9 am to 4 pm daily.

Admission, parking, and local shuttles are all free, making the expo an accessible opportunity for visitors of all ages to experience aviation up close.

Over the past 18 years, the Midwest Aviation Expo has grown into a highly anticipated event at Mt. Vernon Outland Airport, bringing aircraft manufacturers, aviation professionals, pilots and visitors together in Southern Illinois.

Throughout the three-day expo, aircraft will be flying all day, every day, giving attendees the chance to see a diverse collection of MOSAIC aircraft, Light Sport Aircraft (LSAs) and ultralights in action.  Demonstration flights and static aircraft displays will provide additional opportunities to get a closer look at today’s recreational aviation industry.
